fail_first.observed: Scoped missing graph: reserved pivot 409 versus missing pivot 404.
Ordinary unreadable evidence returned 403 instead of 200 with redacted evidence.
Admin batch with an earlier invalid vector returned 404 for a reserved later attachment versus 422 for a missing later attachment.
HTTP feed exposed root and tenant-qualified reserved collection names in nested attached/detached operations.
Reserved named credential scope returned 201 while missing scope returned 404.
Tenant named search returned root record 111 instead of tenant record 222.
Startup accepted default evidence instead of returning the static invalid-bindings error.

resolution_audit.justification: Tenant-qualifies once; ordinary name grant first, reserved check before db.resolve.
T1 fixed: both consume the guarded collection ID, never the unqualified target.
Other handlers retain guarded IDs; disk ANN recovers stored name by ID; provider capture/recheck uses CollectionRef IDs.
Every KV lookup uses tenants::qualify after open_guarded, never an unqualified root name.
Both guard the target, then use the same tenant-qualified stored name.
Imports refuse any nonempty bindings set; otherwise guarded resolution and tenant-qualified re-resolution address the same identity.
D4 fixed: qualify tenant scope, mask reserved named scopes before db.resolve; wildcard provisioning unchanged.
D1/D2 fixed: scoped pivot masking at cover's resolution stage; evidence masking at core retrieval resolution. Ordinary evidence redaction retained.

Scoped body-name grant and reserved checks precede cover as ordinary grants require. Unscoped body names are masked at the core plan_input resolve stage; the remaining best-effort resolve only supplies quotas. F7 delete-node attachment refusal remains for every role.
Server-only visibility callback replaces only reserved-name resolution, at the same stage as missing ordinary collections; embedded and memory writes use the unchanged visible-all wrapper.
All name-based collection lookups use tenants::qualify plus open_qualified. Configured bindings still refuse gRPC startup; change filtering additionally hardened.
Trusted startup binding provisioning resolves stored names after binding validation; not a raw request path.
Exact memory binding/scope authorization precedes ID revalidation; deliberately uses the authorized stored evidence name.
All five named maintenance paths use the guarded ID; legacy paths guard only the default collection.
Direct collection lookups are test fixtures/assertions, not live handler bypasses.

structural_guard_campaign.campaign: Structural guard: hand mutants of the request scope, the guard residues and the generated differential
structural_guard_campaign.protocol: Each mutant replaces exactly one occurrence of `old` by `new` in `file` of the baseline commit; `cmd` runs from the repository root. A mutant is killed when the build succeeds and at least one test the command ran fails because of it. A build error or a command that runs no test is not a kill. The file is restored before the next mutant.
